what: 1000-game paired A/B isolating the NNUE contribution: campaign_v7 cycle-108 arch-v2 (PIENNQ02, h1024) at blend 75 -- the current active model -- against v1 cycle-98 (PIENNQ01, h64) at blend 25, which is the exact model configuration used by every anchor ladder on record. Same binary, same search, --same-search, 500 paired openings with colors reversed, 150 ms/move, Threads=1.
why: No arch-v2 net had ever been measured against anything external. Every ladder number on record (1892 / 2146 / 2422 / S6 +83) used the v1 h64 net at blend 25, so all ten campaign_v7 promotions were unquantified. A paired net-vs-net A/B isolates exactly the unmeasured quantity without needing the anchor, and unlike a ladder it is robust to CPU contention because both arms suffer it symmetrically at fixed movetime.

baseline.note: identical to the configuration measured at 2146 [2087, 2212] on 2026-08-12

search_cost.note: the arch-v2 net wins 71.55% while searching ~0.33 ply SHALLOWER at equal time. Eval quality more than pays for the width.

caveats: This is a CONFOUNDED comparison by design: it moves both the architecture (v1 h64 -> v2 h1024) and the blend (25 -> 75) together. It answers 'how much stronger is the engine now than before', not 'how much did arch-v2 alone buy'.
Measured at 150 ms/move. Every anchor ladder ran at 60+0.5s. Transfer across time control is unverified.
This is an internal delta against one specific opponent. Part of a gain measured against a single predecessor can be opponent-specific and need not transfer fully to Stockfish.

DO NOT simply add 160 to 2146. SF16's UCI_Elo is compressed in this range -- the same binary measured 2146 at rungs 1800/2100 and 2422 at rungs 2400/2700 on the same afternoon. Any anchored number requires a fresh ladder at matched rungs on a matched machine.
supersedes_open_item: The 'no arch-v2 net has ever faced an external measurement' gap is now partly closed. A true anchor ladder on this net at matched rungs is still not done.
